messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran quantized bring-up for Harpoon-11B (int8 + KV cache) on sigma pool. Need product guidance on routing. TL;DR: ~2.4x cost-down vs fp16 but measurable hit on long-turn recall for summarization slice.
aj: Nice. Can you share the numbers?
maria: Quick summary: p50 latency 120ms(fp16) -> 150ms(int8) for seq=256; p95 380ms -> 520ms. Token throughput ~2.2x. Unit cost fp16 = $0.028/1k tokens, int8 = $0.011/1k. BUT rouge-L drop ~3.8 pts on QA/summarization narrowband.
sasha: 3.8 pts is material. Which slices/prompts are worst?
maria: Summarizer (priming-heavy) and multi-turn support threads. eval-bot ran a 5k example batch — link: https://dash.redwood/harpoon11b/quant-5k (internal)
eval-bot: batch eval finished. Results: rougeL_drop: 3.8; help_rate_down: 2.1%; factuality_regress: 0.7%. Observed KV-cache mismatch ~1 per 30 reqs for primed sequences.
oliver: Is degradation concentrated by context length?
maria: Yes. >1024 tokens: rougeL drop ~5.6. <=512 tokens: drop ~1.2. So hybrid routing looks viable: short contexts -> int8, long contexts -> fp16 fallback.
product-lead: Product note: support chat uses long-context ~25% of calls. We can't surface regressions to end users.
aj: Have we tried int6 or quant-aware fine-tune?
maria: Ran small int6 sweep (200 examples): cost about 1.6x int8, quality closer to fp16 (rouge drop ~1.0) but larger p95 variance — tails spike. Not production-ready without more tuning.
tim: What about smaller variant—Harpoon-7B int8? Better trade?
maria: 7B int8 has lower unit cost but recall for multi-turn is worse than 11B fp16. So not a drop-in replacement for support flows.
sasha: Ops approach: hybrid routing + conservative canary. Eg: route <=512 tokens to int8 by default, >1024 to fp16, with shadowing/monitoring on the long tail.
infra-bot: Flag created: deploy/harpoon11b-int8-hybrid-routing. Owner: @maria. Canary rate: 0.5% initial.
maria: Proposed recommendation for GTN: 1) Do not roll out full int8. 2) Canary hybrid routing (rules above). 3) Run 1M-token gating eval with product prompts. 4) Explore int6 selectively for short-turn traffic. 5) Add prompt-rewrite (reduce priming mismatch) as a mitigator.
aj: For GTN, we need a risk-adjusted unit-econ slide. Show current vs hybrid expected costs and expected quality delta.
sasha: Can you paste the cost math?
maria: unit_cost_hybrid = 0.75 * $0.011 + 0.25 * $0.028 = $0.01525 -> ~45% savings vs fp16. Expected rougeL_loss = 0.75 * 1.2 + 0.25 * 5.6 = 2.1 points (approx).
product-lead: 2.1 rougeL is borderline. If prompt-rewrite recovers ~1.0 pt, product OK. Need a small user study to validate.
oliver: Ops checklist for canary: tracing hooks, per-route quality sampling, fallback thresholds, automatic rollback conditions.
maria: Canary runbook draft: perf hooks + per-route sample of 10k requests, automatic rollback if routed_sla breach >3x or net_quality_drop >3 pts on sampled eval. Will stage cook-off with GTN key.
eval-bot: Scheduling 48h shadow job at 2% traffic (100k requests) to collect real traffic signals.
tim: Anything else to surface to GTN?
maria: Timeline: canary deploy tomorrow; 48h shadow + 7-day slow roll if metrics OK. I'll assemble GTN brief with the numbers, slices, and example prompts.
aj: :thumbsup:
sasha: :eyes: include the actual sample prompts and note that prompt-rewrite experiments may alter templates.
product-lead: Assigning GTN doc to @maria and @sasha to finalize.
maria: Will follow up and attach the GTN brief in a new thread.
